result: GNAI2 and GNAI3 are similarly polarized at the hair cell apex with GPSM2, whereas GNAI1 and GNAO are not detected. Immunolabeling with two antibodies (scbt"GNAI3" and pt"GNAI2") showed that both detect GNAI2 and GNAI3 but not GNAI1 at the bare zone and stereocilia tips. GNAO does not contribute to hair cell polarization.
evaluation: Reviewers describe the study as 'highly rigorous and thorough' with 'detailed quantifications' and 'convincing results.' The immunolabeling experiments characterizing GNAI protein localization are part of the comprehensive approach that reviewers praise, with no specific concerns raised about these findings.

result: In Gnai3 mutants, GNAI2 progressively fails to fully occupy the subcellular compartments where GNAI3 is missing. At E18.5, GNAI2 can still occupy the bare zone, but by P0 and P6, GNAI2 shows incomplete and variable enrichment at the bare zone and stereocilia tips. This progressive inability of GNAI2 to compensate explains the variable stereocilia defects in Gnai3 mutants.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state that 'GNAI2 can compensate for GNAI3 loss in early development but incompletely in late development,' directly affirming this finding. The detailed quantifications and temporal analysis are part of the 'depth and care' that reviewers find 'impressive.'

result: GNAI3 is essential for hair bundle morphogenesis and can fully compensate for loss of GNAI2, whereas GNAI2 makes a clear but non-essential contribution. Single Gnai1, Gnai2, or Gnai1; Gnai2 mutants show no overt hair cell defects, while Gnai3 mutants show truncated hair bundles and shortened stereocilia. GNAO is not involved in hair bundle development.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly conclude that 'GNAI3 is the primary GNAI proteins required for hair bundle morphogenesis' and note that 'GNAI3 has the largest effect on hair bundle development.' The comprehensive analysis across multiple mutant lines is praised as 'thorough with detailed quantification.'

result: GNAI3, but not GNAI2, GNAI1, or GNAO, is essential for proper auditory thresholds. Gnai3 mutants show profound deafness at high frequencies (32-40 kHz) and elevated thresholds at lower frequencies, while Gnai1, Gnai2, Gnai1; Gnai2, and Gnao1 mutants show normal ABR thresholds.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm the study's conclusions about auditory function, noting the 'detailed quantification of hair bundle orientation and morphogenesis, as well as auditory functions.' The functional data complement the morphological findings that reviewers find 'convincing.'

result: Simultaneous inactivation of Gnai2 and Gnai3 causes a delay or failure of the basal body to migrate off-center (symmetry breaking defect), with up to 29-34% of hair cells showing symmetrical morphology at E17.5. The bare zone is virtually absent at E17.5 and significantly reduced at P0 in Gnai2; Gnai3 mutants. In contrast, DIO-ptxA mutants show normal symmetry breaking with no symmetrical hair cells, and only a slight delay in bare zone expansion that is progressively corrected.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state that the 'Gnai2 Gnai3 double mutant recapitulates nearly all the phenotypic effects associated with pertussis toxin expression and also reveals a role for GNAIs in early movement of the basal body.' The revised manuscript is noted to have 'clarified the phenotypic differences raised between the Gnai2/3 double mutants and Ptx mutant phenotypes,' resolving previous concerns.

result: Simultaneous inactivation of Gnai2 and Gnai3 causes reversal in the orientation of some hair cell types, particularly OHC1-2. The orientation defects appear with a delay compared to ptxA mutants, with OHC2 initially oriented laterally (90°) before becoming inverted at more mature stages. IHC and OHC3 are severely misoriented in Gnai2; Gnai3 mutants but much less affected in DIO-ptxA mutants.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm that 'hair bundle orientation requires both GNAI2 and GNAI3' and note that the study addresses 'whether all phenotypes resulting from expression of pertussis toxin stemmed from GNAI inhibition.' The comprehensive analysis of orientation defects across developmental stages and positions is part of the 'detailed quantifications' that reviewers praise.

result: There is an allelic series (Gnai3neo < Gnai1neo; Gnai3neo < LSL-myc:ptxA < Foxg1-Cre; Gnai2del; Gnai3flox) along which defects increase in severity. The new DIO-ptxA model produces identical apical hair cell defects to the LSL-myc:ptxA strain, with differences in OHC1 inversion depending on the Cre driver used.
evaluation: Reviewers describe the collection of mouse models as 'impressive and nearly comprehensive' and note that 'appropriate methods were employed' to characterize the phenotypes. The comparison between models is part of the 'depth and care' that reviewers find convincing.

result: Each role of GNAI proteins involves different dosage, specific identity, timing, and upstream regulators. GNAI2 can fully rescue symmetry breaking and orientation when GNAI1 and GNAI3 are absent, but cannot rescue hair bundle morphogenesis. Embryonic activities run on low GNAI/O amounts compared to hair bundle functions. The work reconciles previous reports and validates all hair cell defects observed with ptx as physiologically relevant.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state that the study is 'likely the authoritative last word on which GNAI proteins are needed for which aspect of auditory hair bundle development' and that it 'builds on earlier reports, both uncovering new functions and putting previously putative functions on solid ground.' The comprehensive nature of the conclusions is affirmed by reviewers calling this 'the definitive study.'

result: Background and established knowledge about GNAI proteins, hair cell development, pertussis toxin effects, the EMX2>GPR156>GNAI signaling cascade, GPSM2-GNAI complex function, and the relationship to human deafness genes. These claims provide context for the experimental findings.
evaluation: Reviewers do not question the background information or established knowledge presented. The study is described as building appropriately on previous work, with reviewers noting it 'builds on earlier reports' and addresses 'open questions' in the field.
